info.bio:
Banda formada en los años 80's, surgida de la escena metalera de la bahía de San Francisco, CA.
Conformada originalmente por Les Claypool en el bajo y la voz, Todd Huth en la guitarra  y un ejército de bateristas siendo Jay Lane el que más duró en la etapa pre-estudio del grupo. Para 1989 sacaron el primer disco que fue en vivo, llamado Suck on this, el cual contó con la alineación clásica de Primus que cambió a Huth por Larry LaLonde y a Lane por Tim Alexander.

scenes.name: Funk rock: Chili Peppers, Primus y la Black Rock Coalition
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: A los blancos les era mucho más fácil tocar funk y grabar: Jane’s Addiction debutó con un directo, Primus de Les Claypool (devoto de Larry Graham), los Limbomaniacs con Bootsy y Maceo, Praxis. Los Red Hot Chili Peppers de Anthony Kiedis y Flea, con Freaky Styley producido por Clinton (1985), versionaron a Sly, los Meters y Stevie y llevaron a P-Funk al escenario de los Grammy de 1993; pero los creadores del funk rock, como los P-Funk All Stars, no tenían esa libertad. En Nueva York Living Colour de Vernon Reid no conseguía contrato pese a tener a Mick Jagger de fan, y Reid y Greg Tate fundaron en 1985 la Black Rock Coalition: «El rock and roll es música negra y nosotros somos sus herederos», contra el «rock de orientación apartheid». Abrió paso a Steve Coleman, Me’Shell NdegéOcello, James Blood Ulmer o el Kelvynator de Kelvyn Bell.

scenes.desc: Phish devuelven el rock alternativo a la radio y legitiman el regreso a la estética progresiva, sobre todo en la Costa Este: Blues Traveler, Motherhead Bug y Sulfur, Spin Doctors, Klezmatics, Cul De Sac (Ecim, China Gate) y Run On. El noise-punk-jazz de God Is My Co-pilot, Molecules, Love Child, Blowhole, Harry Pussy. Virginia como epicentro (Echolyn, Boud Deun, Rake, Dave Matthews Band). Solistas: Marc Ribot, Nicky Skopelitis, Buckethead, Loren Mazzacane, los zappianos Ant-Bee y Mike Keneally, Gary Lucas, Alan Licht, Bob Drake. En la Costa Oeste, Primus (Frizzle Fry), Mr Bungle, Amy Denio, Caveman Shoestore, Thessalonians. Internacional: Philharmonie, Xaal, Volapuk, Kevin Martin (God, Techno Animal, Ice, Bug). Y la Babel final: Bright, Meringue, Cerberus Shoal, Tin Hat Trio, Species Being.

podcast.title: 924 Gilman Street Alumni
podcast.body: Primus is identified as an alumnus of 924 Gilman Street, the influential all-ages punk club in West Berkeley, California. The club's rule prohibiting major label bands means that Primus, despite their roots there, is no longer welcome to perform. "Gilman Street alumni like Green Day and the offspring and AFI and Primus and even bad religion aren't really welcome anymore."

podcast.title: Commercial Success and Awards
podcast.body: The band has achieved significant commercial success, with a couple of platinum albums and one gold album. They have also received Grammy nominations on at least two occasions. "Primus is at a couple of platinum albums, one gold album, and it's been nominated for Grammys at least twice."

podcast.title: Concert Etiquette: Yelling "Primus Sucks!"
podcast.body: It is considered good etiquette for audience members to yell "Primus Sucks!" at the band during their live shows, a practice the band reportedly appreciates. "By the way, if you ever go to a Primus show, it is very good etiquette to yell Primus Sucks at the band. That's what you're supposed to do and they're very grateful when you do it."

podcast.title: Instrument Variety
podcast.body: Les Claypool utilizes a range of instruments, including standard four-string basses, six-string basses when needed, and various stand-up basses. "Some of his guitars have the standard four strings. He also plays a six string bass when the knee derises, or if necessary, any variety of stand-up basses."

podcast.title: Les Claypool – Rejected by Metallica for Being "Too Good"
podcast.body: Les Claypool is known for an unmatched and versatile attack on the bass, combining funk, slapping, strumming, and effects — often while singing simultaneously. A widely told anecdote holds that he was deemed "too good" when he auditioned for Metallica. "Combines funk, slapping, strumming, and effects use, with a myth that he was 'too good' for Metallica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Les Claypool's Bass-Driven Style
podcast.body: Primus's music, a mix of alternative metal and funk metal, is primarily built around the distinctive bass grooves of singer and bass player Les Claypool. Claypool is described as an inventive player, unafraid to push boundaries, with a style comparable to Geddy Lee of Rush crossed with Flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "Primus, experiments with a mix of alternative metal and funk metal, all built around singer and bass player Les Claypool's grooves. Great player, very inventive, never afraid to push boundaries."

podcast.title: Unconventional Bass Techniques
podcast.body: Les Claypool is known for his unique and aggressive approach to the bass, which includes rocking out, getting super funky, strumming, slapping, and tapping the strings with his fingers. "He can rock out, he can get super funky, he strums the strings."

podcast.title: Use of Whammy Bar and Effects
podcast.body: Some of Les Claypool's basses are equipped with a whammy bar, allowing him to bend notes in unusual ways. He also processes his notes through a series of processors and distortion pedals to achieve diverse sounds. "Some of his guitars have a whammy bar, which is really weird, so he can bend notes in unusual ways."

podcast.title: Winona Ryder Controversy
podcast.body: Despite the song "Winona's Big Brown Beaver" not being about actress Winona Ryder, its release sparked a feud with Ryder and her then-boyfriend, Dave Perner of Solosalam, who were "not very impressed." "They once released a single called Winona's Big Brown Beaver, which is not about actress Winona Ryder, but she and her boyfriend at the time, Dave Perner of Solosalam, were not very impressed with this, and there was something of a feud for a while."

xref.title: The Residents (Shreveport LA, 1969) – No Known Members; Hardy W. Fox Died 2018 Listed as Co-Founder; George Harrison and Claypool Denied
xref.body: The Residents are an art collective that originated in Shreveport, Louisiana in 1969. By 1971 they were performing in San Francisco. They have never shown their faces or listed any band members — their only point of contact is a company called Cryptic Music. When their debut album Meet the Residents was released in 1974 (parodying the Beatles' Meet the Beatles), some fans believed they were actually the Beatles in disguise. Hardy W. Fox — who claimed to have been a Resident — died in 2018 with his obituary listing him as co-founder and primary songwriter. Other names tied to the band include Homer Cook (unconfirmed), Jay Clem (maybe), and "Charles Boebuck" (apparently a pseudonym for Fox). Contrary to rumors, George Harrison, Les Claypool of Primus, and no member of Devo has ever been in the band. "I can tell you, though, contrary to rumors, George Harrison less clay pool of primus, and no one from Devo has ever been in the residence."

xref.title: 924 Gilman Street Alumni
xref.body: Green Day are alumni of the all-ages punk club 924 Gilman Street in West Berkeley, California. They were welcome there during their early "indie days," including when they recorded an original song in 1992. However, due to the club's strict rule against major label bands, Green Day is no longer permitted to play there, along with other successful punk acts. "Gilman Street alumni like Green Day and the offspring and AFI and Primus and even bad religion aren't really welcome anymore."

xref.title: Groundbreaking Funk Metal Sound
xref.body: Living Colour, a band of four Black men from New York City, created a funk metal sound that laid the groundwork for many groups of the 1990s. Their influence was felt across bands like Rage Against the Machine, 311, Primus, and even Korn. "The resulting funk metal laid the groundwork for many groups of the 1990s, ranging from rage against the machine to 311 to primus to even corn."
